text:
B: Now then.
A: Hi. Adam. Shipley, near Bradford.
B: Gary. Hucknall. You're the stonemason.
A: Er, yeah. Word's got round, then.
B: Elira said. Proper trade, that. Not many of you left.
A: No. There's not. Most of the lads at our place are over fifty. We've got two apprentices, but that's about it round here.
B: Same in ours. Nobody wants to learn owt properly. They want the money without the years.
A: Er, some of them are alright, to be fair. They just need showing.
B: Hm. Maybe. What d'you do, then, new stone or old?
A: Old, mostly. Repairs on sandstone, chapels, mills, terraces. Cutting new blocks to match and fixing them in, repointing in lime.
B: Lime. I'd have thought cement were stronger.
A: It is stronger, that's the problem. Er, if the mortar's harder than the stone, the stone takes all the movement and the water. So it cracks and the face blows instead of the joint. You want the joint to be the weak bit, so you can rake it out and do it again in fifty years.
B: Never thought of it like that.
A: Most people don't. You see it everywhere round Bradford, terraces done in cement in the eighties.
B: I put an extension on ours, back in the day. Brick, mind, not stone. Did it myself with a mate. Twenty year and not a crack in it.
A: That's good going. Brick's a lot more forgiving, mind.
B: You what? Laid it level, that's what. You doing football, you a City man?
A: Bradford City, yeah. Go with my dad, a few home games a season.
B: Notts County. We've had our share of rubbish an' all.
A: Ha. City's been a bit rubbish this year. I mostly go for my dad, really. He's semi-retired now, it's our thing.
B: That's right, that. My lad set me up a stream, but it's not the same as going.
A: No. The pies are better at the ground.
B: Pies are better at ours. What did your dad do?
A: Lorry driver. Thirty-odd years.
B: Mine were at the pit, Linby, till it shut. Then nothing for years. Taught me to keep money put by.
A: Yeah. I'm trying. Saving for a house, I'm back at my mum and dad's.
B: Nowt wrong with that. Get it paid off quick, that's the trick. I'll have mine done in two year.
A: That's good going.
B: You do any work on the side? I do fences, sheds, cash.
A: Er, a bit. Neighbours' walls now and then. Mostly I'm sketching stone in a notebook, if I'm honest. Not very profitable.
B: Ha. No. Do the walls, then.
